enum.name: SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT_FLAGS
enum.description: Status and switch flags for SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT.

entry.name: SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT_FLAGS_FAILSAFE
entry.description: The link upstream of the sender is in failsafe: the forwarded input is stale or synthesized, not live operator input. The flight controller treats this like any RC failsafe.

enum.name: SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT_AUX_SWITCHES
enum.description: Two-position auxiliary switches aux06-aux12 of SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT, one bit each.

message.name: SD_CONTROLLER_INPUT
message.description: Controller input sent by a ground control station, one stream per physical link, routed unmodified to the flight controller (typically MAVLink over UDP to a companion computer acting as MAVLink router, then MAVLink over USB/serial to the FC - the router never parses or muxes). The GCS tags each stream itself: links carrying the same operator's controls share a controller_id (e.g. the LoRa link and the IP-radio link of one transmitter); link_id identifies the redundant link within that controller and doubles as the flight controller's selection priority (lower wins). The payload is the Sweden Dynamics packed controller frame, as defined for the Gungnir radio link and reused on every input path so the flight controller's input mux sees one format: four 10-bit stick channels, two 8-bit, one 3-bit and two 2-bit auxiliary channels, seven two-position auxiliary switches, and the ARMED and E-stop switches carried in flags. A stick value of UINT16_MAX means that channel carries no data; the auxiliary channels always carry data. Nominal rate 50 Hz per link.
message.field: System ID of the vehicle to control (0 for broadcast).
Physical controller this input belongs to. Controller 0 is the primary operator.
Redundant link within the controller; selection priority (lower wins).
Per-link frame counter, wraps at 255. Set at the origin, so gaps measure loss anywhere along the GCS-to-FC path.
Link status flags and the ARMED / E-stop switches.
Stick channels chn01-chn04, 10-bit, 0-1023. UINT16_MAX = channel not present.
Auxiliary channel aux01, 8-bit, 0-255.
Auxiliary channel aux02, 8-bit, 0-255.
Auxiliary channel aux03, 3-bit, 0-7.
Auxiliary channel aux04, 2-bit, 0-3.
Auxiliary channel aux05, 2-bit, 0-3.
Two-position auxiliary switches aux06-aux12, one bit each.
Link quality of this link, 0-100. UINT8_MAX: unknown.
RSSI of this link in dBm (negative). INT8_MAX: unknown.

message.name: SD_OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD
message.description: Optical flow from the companion-computer vision pipeline, one message per frame pair, with the companion's height above ground and its uncertainty, sent atomically. The sender is a body-FRD virtual nadir sensor (consumer must set its flow rotation to none) whose flow is already rotation-compensated: there are no gyro integrals, and the consumer must not compensate with its own gyro (treat the sensor's rotation as zero). Refused frame pairs are sent with flow_sigma NaN rather than as gaps, so no-data and bad-data stay distinguishable. Rate follows the frame pairing, up to the camera's decoded frame rate.
message.field: Trailing edge of the flow integration interval, stamped at the later frame's exposure time on the sender's clock. The consumer must convert clocks via TIMESYNC and must not re-center: it applies the mid-interval correction itself.
Sensor ID. 0 is the primary vision pipeline.
Integration interval between the frame pair. Reported honestly on refused pairs too, so the stream stays continuous.
Flow around X axis. Sensor linear motion along the positive Y axis induces a negative flow. Rotation already removed by the sender.
Flow around Y axis. Sensor linear motion along the positive X axis induces a positive flow. Rotation already removed by the sender.
1-sigma uncertainty of the flow rate (integrated_x and integrated_y divided by integration_time_us), per axis. NaN: refused pair, no valid flow (still sent, never a gap).

Height above ground level: vertical height of the sensor above the visible surface below it (ground, or canopy where that is what the camera sees) - not a slant range along the sensor axis. From the companion's own height source (map height, estimator, terrain matching), valid at time_usec. -1: unknown.
1-sigma uncertainty of hagl. NaN: unknown.
